label: r4c2
name: 1 epoch, higher lr
hypothesis: Same network as r3c1, with ppo_epochs 1 (about 367k samples) and lr raised from 0.001 to 0.002. One epoch moves the policy less per update; doubling the learning rate makes up for that and speeds the early escape from pressing DONE at once, while the larger sample count is kept. PPO clipping limits instability. Refuted if it scores clearly below the 1-epoch version at lr 0.001, or below r3c1's 0.699 by more than seed noise.
last_analysis: Every trial without a circular row convolution on the target channels scored 0: the agent learned to press DONE at once. The circular (1, X) convolution unlocked learning (r2c1: 0.447). The generic axial version (0.325) and ent_coef 0.05 (0.339) were no better, given the seed noise. Halving PPO epochs from 4 to 2 nearly doubled the samples and gave the clearest gain (r3c1: 0.699, training success still rising at 0.675). So the run is short of samples, not of optimisation per sample. The missing/extra pooling for the DONE head did not help (0.404, and 0.297 with 2 epochs, where one seed scored 0.078). Seed spread is large, up to about 0.44 between seeds. In this final round I push the sample-count lever further, to 1 PPO epoch (about 367k steps), and test a higher learning rate and more frequent smaller updates on top of it. The architecture stays fixed at r3c1, the best so far.
